definitions.explanation: The quantity of matter in a body, a fundamental property in physics. Distinguished from weight, which varies with gravity. Composed of 質 (quality/substance) + 量 (quantity).

examples.japanese: この{物体|ぶったい}の{質量|しつりょう}は{五|ご}キログラムだ。
examples.english: The mass of this object is five kilograms.

examples.japanese: {月|つき}では{重力|じゅうりょく}が{弱|よわ}いが、{質量|しつりょう}は{変|か}わらない。
examples.english: Gravity is weaker on the moon, but mass doesn't change.

examples.japanese: {太陽|たいよう}の{質量|しつりょう}は{地球|ちきゅう}の{約|やく}{三十三万|さんじゅうさんまん}{倍|ばい}もある。
examples.english: The mass of the sun is about 330,000 times that of the earth.

notes:
USAGE:
{質量|しつりょう} is a scientific term used in physics, chemistry, and related fields. In everyday language, {重|おも}さ (weight) is more commonly used, though technically {質量|しつりょう} and {重|おも}さ are different concepts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {質量|しつりょう}を{測|はか}る (measure the mass)
- {原子|げんし}{質量|しつりょう} (atomic mass)
- {質量|しつりょう}{保存|ほぞん}の{法則|ほうそく} (law of conservation of mass)
- {質量|しつりょう}の{単位|たんい} (unit of mass)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{重量|じゅうりょう} means "weight" — the force exerted by gravity on an object. {体重|たいじゅう} means "body weight." In everyday speech, {重|おも}さ covers both mass and weight informally.
